role: Galois layer: the joint Frobenius of p in the compositum of genus/ray class fields of small levels
missing_theorem: There is a Frobenius class 𝒞 in K_T = compositum of ℚ(√−t, ζ_t), t ≤ T, such that Frob_p ∈ 𝒞 alone guarantees a certificate, and these classes cover all Mordell-hard Frobenius classes.
status_ref: CLASS_FORCING Thm 2.1/5.2 ((J)93): Frobenius in a finite Galois extension sees only p mod t, and no class is forbidden for a single large factor; (J)96 (non-abelian Frobenius inert on finite witness sets). Classes guaranteeing a certificate by Galois data alone are exactly the congruence-covered ones (Mordell's non-square classes); on Mordell-hard primes (squares mod 840) they guarantee nothing.
barrier: B1 (Galois data = congruence data); reciprocity forces parity, never class
next: None.
note: The item's own separation (Galois layer vs factorisation layer) is right; the Galois layer is empty on the hard set.

role: interval (Bohr-set) relaxation of the five-slice set L₃(p) plus Burgess in short intervals
missing_theorem: ES₅(p) needs a non-residue A in L₃(p) with exact landing (A = (p+u)/v with the five-slice divisibility). The interval relaxation 'some integer A in ∪_v (p/v, (p+U)/v] is a non-residue' is easy (Burgess for intervals of length > p^{1/4+ε}) but drops the second divisibility condition, which is the B2 event.
yield: ES via ES₅ (only with exact landing)
status_ref: Forest form: five-slice certificates = bichromatic edges uv | p + u + v (LOWER_TAIL_ASTRA); FRONTIER §7.2
barrier: B2 (exact landing = divisor condition); B3 (L₃(p) has (log p)² elements, intervals have power length)
next: None. The interval structure gives where the candidates lie, not which of them land.
note: Every integer A in (p/v, (p+U)/v] has u = Av − p ≤ U; the extra five-slice divisibility is what makes L₃ thin.

role: almost-prime levels: 4Cp+1 = q₁q₂ and the class of q₁ mod 4C
missing_theorem: For every large p there is C ≤ K(p) with 4Cp+1 = q₁q₂ (q_i prime) and q₁ ≡ −1 (mod 4C). A Chen-type lower-bound sieve in C gives many P₂ levels (for K a power of p); the class condition on the private large prime q₁ is the lottery.
status_ref: Pass 1 U03: among (p, C) with Ω(N_C) = 2 the success rate is 0.020 vs 0.051 overall (P₂ levels are worse); CLASS_FORCING Thm 5.2 (no class forbidden for a single large factor)

role: twist a pointwise-true divisor-in-AP asymptotic (modulus 4p) by the self-referential class d ≡ −1 (mod 4C)
missing_theorem: Σ_{C≤X} τ(4Cp+1) has an asymptotic for X ≥ p^{1/2+ε} (divisor function in progressions to modulus 4p up to x^{2/3−ε}, x = 4Xp). Needed: Σ_{C≤X} #{d | 4Cp+1 : d ≡ −1 (mod 4C)} = M_X(p)(1 + o(1)) (or ≥ εM_X(p)). The twist modulus 4C = (n − 1)/p depends on the summation variable n.
status_ref: Two-sided pointwise asymptotics with a polylog main term are false infinitely often (BM_CORRECTED_COUNT Prop 3.1, via Linnik) (for the two-sided form at X = p/4); the one-sided form is H⁻_BM restricted to C ≤ X (circular). PARITY_AUDIT Remark 3.1: every result beating Weil averages over a variable independent of the modulus.
barrier: tied modulus
next: None as an ES route. A clean §7.1-type sub-question: any non-trivial bound for the twisted sum with C ≤ p^{1/2+ε} beyond the divisor bound.
note: The base asymptotic is pointwise in p, but it is the class twist that carries all the difficulty.

role: Linnik's ergodic method with an auxiliary split prime ℓ (e.g. the least non-residue) acting on ES certificates
missing_theorem: There is an ℓ-adic group (Hecke correspondence) acting on the set of certificates of p, e.g. on SL₂ certificates [[a, p], [c, d]], whose orbits are large and equidistribute; Linnik/ELMV then force a certificate in the target region.
status_ref: No such action: ES integral points have a finite automorphism group (thin_group_orbits §3; WINDMILL Prop 2, order 4), no Vieta involutions (cayley_markoff_cm P3), and Hecke operators of degree ℓ change the determinant, so they leave the set of SL₂ certificates. FRONTIER §3 M-table: M3 (homogeneity) is the input B2 lacks.
barrier: M3 (no group action); B3 (Linnik/Duke counts are power-size)
next: None.
note: The BM layer is already pointwise free by the least non-residue (SYNTHESIS_SPARKS9); there is no dynamics to push it further.

role: existence by equidistribution of always-existing objects (CM points / closed geodesics of discriminant tied to p)
missing_theorem: There is a family of objects attached to p (CM points of discriminant −16p or −4(4Cp+1), closed geodesics of discriminant p) and a region Ω_p with: object in Ω_p ⟺ ES certificate; and effective equidistribution at the scale of μ(Ω_p).

ET Thm 1.1): an encoding with fibres ≤ p^{o(1)} has target main term ≤ p^{o(1)}, so μ(Ω_p) ≈ p^{−1+o(1)}, while Duke/subconvexity resolve only regions of measure ≥ p^{−δ}. FRONTIER §6 (Heegner/CM small-scale equidistribution → B3); BRAINSTORM/z9_heegner_layers.md

role: interpolate between 4-term (trivial) and 3-term ES by constrained many-variable families accessible to the circle method
missing_theorem: There is a constrained family F of 4-term representations (e.g. 1/z + 1/w = 1/v) with (i) F(n) ≠ ∅ ⇒ ES(n), and (ii) a circle-method main term at fixed n of power size with a smaller error.
status_ref: B3 (CONDITIONAL_ES Prop 2.3): an F-solution maps to a 3-term solution with fibres ≤ μ(n), so #F(n) ≤ μ(n)·f(n). Natural merge constraints have μ = τ(v²) = n^{o(1)}, so the count is n^{o(1)} on average; the circle method needs M1a (power counts). Families with power-size fibres would need a free parameter not seen by the 3-term solution, and then (i) fails or the fibres are trivial.
barrier: B3; M1a
next: None. Recording: 'k-term ES with constraints implying 3-term ES' inherits the 3-term count up to fibre size.
note: The interesting step (implication to 3-term) is exactly what keeps the count small.

role: certificate scheme whose only hard condition is primality of linear forms in auxiliary variables (Green–Tao–Ziegler, as in Harpaz–Skorobogatov–Wittenberg)
missing_theorem: For every large p there is a finite system of linear forms L_i(t) (coefficients depending on p) with: ∃ t in a box where all L_i(t) are prime ⇒ ES(p); and a GTZ-type count giving ≥ 1 such t.
status_ref: B3 counting: the scheme maps prime tuples injectively (up to p^{o(1)}) to ES solutions, so the expected number of tuples is ≤ f(p)·p^{o(1)} = p^{o(1)} on average (ET Thm 1.1). A GTZ main term T/(log T)^k is that small only if the box T is polylog while the coefficients are poly(p) — far outside GTZ uniformity (Z3135). B-fin: ES at fixed p is a finite search with certifying moduli O(p²).
barrier: B3; B-fin; uniformity of GTZ in the coefficients
next: None.
note: Thm C (H ⇒ bounded witness procedures fail) does not forbid such schemes; the count does.

role: Deuring–Heilbronn-type dichotomy: if (·/p) is 'exceptional' (QR at all small primes) other certificate families become abundant
missing_theorem: Two pointwise theorems: (A) if lnr(p) ≤ L then R(p) ≥ 1 (BM layer positive at some level ≤ 4L); (B) if lnr(p) > L then some other family (b = 1 line, windows) has a certificate.
status_ref: Neither half is known. Data: the 14 (★)-failures ≤ 10¹⁰ have least non-residue 5, 5, 7, 7, 7, 11, 13, 13, 13, 13, 17, 19, 23, 23 (this pass, script (3)), so (★)-hardness is not concentrated on exceptional p; RESIDUE_HARDNESS: hardness is 'p ≡ 1 mod many small q' (practical p − 1). BRAINSTORM/z45_siegel_dichotomy.md, hardness_law.md
barrier: B2 in both halves; for (A), sterile points on lnr-r lines for r ≥ 2^{21.44} ((J)70) show that even 'lnr small' needs non-congruence input
next: Compare, on primes with lnr(p) ≥ 17 vs controls, the counts of (★), b = 1 and window certificates (Pass 1 never ran this). If no family gets richer, the dichotomy has no 'repelled' side.
note: Linnik/Heilbronn repulsion is an analytic property of L-function zeros; ES certificates are not zeros, and nothing repels.

role: Dirichlet-type positivity: a combination of character-twisted level series with nonnegative coefficients whose p-th coefficient is forced positive
missing_theorem: There are weights w_t, c_χ with a(n) = Σ_t w_t Σ_χ c_χ σ_χ(tn+1) ≥ 0 for all n, a(n) = 0 ⟹ R(n) = 0, and a(p) > 0 provable for every large prime p.
status_ref: Dirichlet's trick controls a value at s = 1 (a weighted average of all coefficients), not one coefficient. Forcing one coefficient positive is the original problem. T1: by Thm K every such level series vanishes exactly at n = m², so the forcing must see the quadratic character (METAPLECTIC_ES Thm K; (J)7 Thm 9.1: no finite fixed-level Eisenstein identity certifies Type I/II counts).
barrier: B6 (values of Dirichlet series are averages); T1
next: None.
note: Nonnegativity of coefficients is automatic (they are counts); what Dirichlet needs in addition is a pole, which constrains averages only.

role: Erdős–Bertrand size contradiction: ES failure confines every 4Cp+1 (C ≤ X) to thin multiplicative sets S_C; compare with the CRT prime census of Π_C(4Cp+1)
missing_theorem: For large p, the conditions 4Cp+1 ∈ S_C for all C ≤ X (S_C = {N : no divisor ≡ −1 (mod 4C)}) contradict the known size and small-prime content of Π_{C≤X}(4Cp+1).
status_ref: Every prime N ≡ 1 (mod 4C) lies in S_C, so S_C imposes no size constraint on the large-prime part. The small-prime content (q ≤ 4X) is fixed by CRT and is the same at square-mimicking p (where T1 gives failure at every level); large primes are private to one C (SYNTHESIS_SPARKS8 Lemma 2.3). EXSET_SHIFT_DIVISORS.md, PRIMITIVE_INTERSECTION.md
barrier: privacy of large primes; B1 for the small-prime part
next: None.
note: Erdős's argument works because the absence of primes in (n, 2n] makes the binomial coefficient too small; ES failure does not make anything too small.
